transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I'm here because... for the last year or so, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is messing with my dad's lab results. They're either changing them or holding parts back. And it's just... it's wearing me down. No matter how many doctors or even my own family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know what I saw. The chart doesn't match. 

And you know, as a phlebotomist, I see charts all day. I draw blood, I label the vials, I send them off. Just the other day, actually, we had this new guy start at the lab, and he kept putting the labels on crooked. It drove me crazy because if it goes into the machine crooked, it can jam the whole thing. I had to show him like three times how to line it up with the ridge on the tube. It's not that hard, you just have to pay attention. But people don't pay attention anymore, do they? They just rush through everything. Kind of like how they rush through the grocery store. I was at the store yesterday and this woman just left her cart right in the middle of the aisle while she went to look at the pasta sauce. Just left it there! I had to squeeze past her with my basket. 

But anyway, yeah, the numbers on my dad's chart... they just aren't right, and nobody will listen to me.
Can you tell me more about why you believe someone is changing or withholding your dad's lab results, even though doctors have told you they are fine?

Well, it's because I *saw* it. I know what I saw. About a year ago, I was looking at his patient portal, and the hemoglobin levels... they were different than what they printed out at his actual appointment. Someone went in and altered them. Or they deleted a second page, I don't know, but they are holding something back. And it's just... it's exhausting trying to prove it for a whole year. It really wears you down. 

Speaking of being worn down, my shoes are completely falling apart. I work on my feet all day at the clinic, drawing blood, and you'd think they'd give us a shoe allowance or something. My coworker, Sarah—she just bought these really expensive clogs, like the ones chefs wear? She says they're amazing, but they look so heavy. I don't know how she walks in them. I tried wearing clogs once when I was in college, taking this biology prerequisite, and I tripped going up the stairs to the lecture hall. Spilled my coffee everywhere. It was one of those caramel macchiatos, too, the really sticky ones. 

But anyway, yeah, the doctors and my mom and my sister keep saying, "Oh, the numbers are fine, his kidneys are fine," but they don't understand how the system works. They don't see how easy it is for someone to just go in and change a chart. I know they're messing with it.
Have you ever had times when your thoughts felt disorganized or when it was hard to keep your ideas in order?

No, I don't think my thoughts are disorganized. I mean, I know exactly what I'm talking about when it comes to my dad's chart. Everything makes perfect sense to me, it's just that no one else is paying attention. 

Although, speaking of keeping things in order, you should see the supply closet at work. It is a complete disaster. I spent like two hours last week trying to organize the butterfly needles by gauge, because people just throw them in there wherever. It's like they don't even care that we have a system. The blue ones were mixed in with the green ones, and someone had put a whole box of tourniquets right on top of the alcohol prep pads. It’s so frustrating. I told the office manager, Brenda, about it, and she just nodded and went back to eating her yogurt. She always eats that Greek yogurt with the fruit on the bottom, but she never stirs it. She just eats the plain yogurt off the top and leaves the fruit. Who does that? It’s the best part! I buy the big tubs of vanilla and put my own fresh strawberries in it. Strawberries were actually on sale at the farmer's market this weekend. 

But yeah, my thoughts are fine. I'm just trying to get someone to look at the real numbers.
Have you ever had beliefs that others didn't share, that turned out to be completely wrong?

No, I mean... I've never been completely wrong about something big like this. People might not agree with me, but that doesn't mean I'm wrong. I'm usually very observant. Like, I notice things other people just walk right past. 

Actually, that reminds me of this time I was walking my dog, Buster—he's a beagle mix, very stubborn—and we were walking past this house on the corner of Elm and 4th. And I noticed their sprinkler system was on, but it was raining. Pouring, really. And I thought, why would you have your sprinklers on in a downpour? It’s just a waste of water. And water bills in this city are getting ridiculous. I got mine last month and it was almost double what I usually pay. I called the utility company to ask about it, and the guy on the phone—I think his name was Gary—he was so unhelpful. He kept putting me on hold to check the meter reading, and the hold music was this awful, static-y jazz. I don't even like jazz. My ex-boyfriend loved it, used to drag me to these smoky little clubs downtown where everyone wore fedoras and snapped instead of clapping. It was so pretentious. 

But no, I don't have beliefs that turn out to be wrong. I know what I saw on that chart.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that others said weren’t true, but you still felt certain were real?

No, I really haven't. I mean, my dad's chart is the only thing that people are being so stubborn about. I don't go around just making things up. I'm a very grounded person. 

Speaking of being grounded, I actually tried getting into gardening last spring to, you know, stay grounded. I bought all these terracotta pots and this special organic soil that smelled terrible, like fish emulsion or something. I planted tomatoes—heirloom ones, because the ones at the grocery store just taste like water. But the squirrels got to every single one of them before they even ripened. They would just take one bite out of a green tomato and leave it on the patio. It’s so disrespectful! I tried putting cayenne pepper around the pots because someone on a gardening blog said it deters them, but then it rained and washed it all away. Rain has just been ruining everything lately. Like last week, I left my car windows cracked because it was so hot, and this sudden thunderstorm just rolled in out of nowhere. My passenger seat was soaked. It took three days to dry out, and now it smells like wet dog, even though Buster hasn't been in the car for a month. 

But anyway, no, I don't have other beliefs like that. Just the truth about the lab results.

Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something strongly that others said wasn’t true, even when there was clear evidence against it—like seeing, hearing, or knowing things that others didn’t seem to understand?

No, no, it's not like that. I don't just make things up or imagine things. I'm here because for the past year, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. And I know what I saw. No matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I saw, and it's just wearing me down. 

It's exhausting, honestly. Kind of like how tired I get after working a double shift at the clinic. We had three call-outs last Tuesday, and I was running between the pediatric wing and oncology all day. Kids are so hard to draw blood from, you know? They squirm so much. There was this one little boy, maybe four years old, wearing these light-up dinosaur shoes. Every time he stomped, they flashed red and green. It reminded me of Christmas, which is just around the corner, really. I still haven't bought a gift for my sister. She's impossible to shop for. Last year I got her a cashmere sweater, and she said it made her itch. Who complains about cashmere? It was expensive, too. I got it at that boutique downtown, the one next to the bakery that makes those amazing almond croissants. They flake everywhere when you eat them, but they're so good with a cup of dark roast coffee. 

But yeah, I'm not imagining things. The chart is wrong, and I just need someone to actually look at it and see what I see.
